Israel’s Eisenkot warns Netanyahu against ‘dangerous moves’ before new government takes office
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming Israel’s next government, warned caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu against launching military or security operations without an immediate threat, Israeli media reported Wednesday. In a letter to Netanyahu, Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, said the prime minister was heading a caretaker government that no longer enjoyed the confidence of the Knesset, Israel’s parliament, according to the Ynet news website. “Only 46 Knesset members still support your continued tenure as prime minister,” said Eisenkot. item.title: US watchdog expose Israeli intelligence links with Sudan’s RSF
item.description: Midas Project, the US-based organisation, exposed this Tuesday that a network of 400 sockpuppet accounts on the X platform was found to advance the cause of many entities, including the RSF militia.  The network traced back to Koios, the Israeli intelligence company, which claimed it stopped its business last year, but at the same time, a new company with the same staff and business model appeared. The account associated with Koios kept posting online.  Accounts affiliated with the network shared tweets claiming the RSF militia is pro-peace and pro-ceasefire, and that it works to promote stability and protect civilians, end local rivalries, and facilitate humanitarian access. In addition to accusing the Sudanese Army of having ties with the Muslim Brotherhood.  […]

item.title: The beginning of the end: Israel at the heart of America’s political civil war
item.description: On the very morning of the critical US midterm elections, President Donald Trump made what seemed like a shocking announcement: no more aid to Israel. “Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4 billion a year, and we made a deal months ago that we’re stopping,” Trump told Fox News’ Fox & Friends. He goes on to make two seemingly contradictory assertions: “We won’t be paying Israel,” and “We’ll help Israel if they need it.” In truth, there was little euphoria among those who have long campaigned against US funding of Israel. item.title: Israeli settlement council chief denied entry to France: Report
item.description: French authorities denied entry to the head of the settlement council in the northern occupied West Bank, in what Israeli media described as a “diplomatic precedent.” i24NEWS, citing his office, said French immigration authorities stopped Yossi Dagan at a Paris airport after he arrived for meetings with elected French officials. The broadcaster said there was no known previous case of a Western country directly barring the head of an Israeli regional council in the occupied West Bank. Dagan’s office said immigration officials took him aside for questioning at passport control last week.
